Version %2$s, %1$s
Start again to update to version %3$s
Start by connecting to a computer
For devices without root, you need to use adb to start aMiNo (requires computer connection). This process needs to be repeated every time the device is restarted. Please read the help.

%1$s

* There are some other considerations, please confirm that you have read the help first.

On Android 11 or above, you can enable Wireless debugging and start aMiNo directly from your device, without connecting to a computer.

Please view the step-by-step guide first.
Before Android 11, connecting to a computer is required to enable Wireless debugging.

Please enable \"Wireless debugging\" in \"Developer options\". \"Wireless debugging\" is automatically disabled when network changes.\n\nNote, do not disable \"Developer options\" or \"USB debugging\", or aMiNo will be stopped.
Please try to disable and enable \"Wireless debugging\" if it keeps searching.
Port is an integer ranging from 1 to 65535.
Can\'t connect to wireless debugging service.\n\nPlease ensure that aMiNo is whitelisted in all firewall, ad-block, VPN, or similar apps that can restrict network access.
Wireless debugging is not enabled.\nNote, before Android 11, to enable wireless debugging, computer connection is a must.
USB debugging is not enabled.\nPlease enable it in \"Developer Options\".

Please start pairing by performing the following steps:
- Navigate to "Developer Options"
- Enable "USB debugging" and "Wireless debugging"
- Tap the left side of "Wireless debugging"
- Tap "Pair device with pairing code"
- Input the pairing code in the notification

On Android 14, installing/updating aMiNo with the Package Installer revokes the ^1 permission, which is required to enable the accessibility service for pairing.

To grant it, run the following ADB command:

^2

After running the command, you may continue with the pairing process.

Note: you can bypass this by installing/updating aMiNo with ADB.

Please enable the accessibility service to start the pairing process. This allows aMiNo to detect the pairing code.\n\nThe accessibility service will be turned off when the code is found or after 1 minute to save energy.

Please start pairing by performing the following steps:
- Navigate to "Developer Options"
- Enable "USB debugging" and "Wireless debugging"
- Tap the left side of "Wireless debugging"
- Tap "Pair device with pairing code." aMiNo will automatically detect the pairing code.
The system requires the pairing dialog to always be visible. Using split-screen mode is the only way to let this app and the system dialog be visible at the same time.
Unable to generate key for wireless debugging.\nThis may be because the KeyStore mechanism of this device is broken.
Failed to stop ADB over TCP
Please go through the pairing step first.
A notification from aMiNo will help you complete the pairing.
Navigate to \"Developer Options\", then enable \"USB debugging\" and \"Wireless debugging\".
Tap the left side of \"Wireless debugging\", then tap \"Pair device with pairing code.\" Enter the code in the notification to complete pairing.
The pairing process needs you to interact with a notification from aMiNo. Please allow aMiNo to post notifications.
MIUI users may need to switch notification style to \"Android\" from \"Notification\" - \"Notification shade\" in system settings.
Otherwise, you may not able to enter the pairing code from the notification.
Go back to aMiNo and start aMiNo.
aMiNo needs to access the local network. It is controlled by the network permission.

Some systems (such as MIUI) disallow apps to access the network when they are not visible, even if the app uses a foreground service. Please disable battery optimization features for aMiNo on such systems.
If you are using Magisk, you can try %1$s. For root users, it will eventually replace aMiNo. Note, existing applications need to change a little to use %2$s.
Apps that have requested or declared the aMiNo permission will show here.
Apps like Tasker and MacroDroid can send intents to start/stop aMiNo automatically.
To use the start intent on your device, you first need to enable ADB over TCP by running %1$s from a PC.
You will need to reconfigure your intents with the new token.
Note: Enabling this feature may cause apps that rely on aMiNo to stop functioning correctly.
Learn how to develop with aMiNo
You need to take an extra step

Your device manufacturer has restricted adb permissions and apps using aMiNo will not work properly.

Usually, this limitation can be lifted by adjusting some options in "Developer options". Please read the help for details on how to do this.

You may need to restart aMiNo for the operation to take effect.
A device reboot is required for aMiNo to work properly. To continue, please reboot your device.
Another version of this app is installed on your device. To continue, please uninstall all duplicate versions and reboot your device.
The permission of adb is limited

It\'s highly possible that your device manufacturer limits the permission of adb.

There may be a solution for your system in this document.
Run shell commands in terminal apps through aMiNo
Users have reported that MIUI breaks the Storage Access Framework, which is used by the export function.
If you are using MIUI, you may have to extract the file from the assets folder in aMiNo\'s APK.
Export the files to a new folder.
Two files will be exported: %1$s and %2$s. If the files already exist in the selected folder, they will be deleted.
Use your terminal app to copy the files to its private files directory.

Tip: If your terminal app\'s home directory (~) is in the private files directory, placing the files there will allow you to run %1$s without writing the path.\n\nOtherwise, you can create an alias for %2$s in your terminal app\'s %3$s configuration file.
Open a shell with the following command:

With %1$s, you can run shell commands in any terminal app.

Tap to learn more about how to use it.
Some apps that use aMiNo may not work when aMiNo is hidden because they try to detect if aMiNo is installed.
As a workaround, you can temporarily unhide aMiNo, which installs a stub with the original package name. When you are finished, you can re-hide aMiNo.
Tap this card to copy a code snippet you can send to the developer so their \"aMiNo installed\" check will work when aMiNo is hidden.
Some apps may still be able to detect aMiNo even when hidden.
You will need to re-pair and re-configure aMiNo after installing the hidden version.
Rish users: re-export the files after installing the hidden version.
Intent users: update your intents with the new package name.
You must update aMiNo through the app when using the hidden version because it has a different signature.
If left empty, a random suffix will be added to the package name.
Package name cannot end with a period.
Only letters, numbers, and periods are allowed.
Package name must have at least two segments.
Segments cannot start with a number.
Choose a folder where the new APK will be saved.
The system will now prompt you to uninstall aMiNo. Then, install the clone.

Due to a bug in Android 11-12, wireless debugging does not remember any authorized networks.\n\nYou will need to re-authorize the network on each reboot by tapping \"Allow\" when the authorization dialog pops up.
Automatically restart aMiNo if it crashes
"Allows aMiNo to restart without Wi-Fi. (aMiNo must have started once since reboot)"
"The TCP port will be closed immediately. You will need Wi-Fi to turn on TCP mode again. Continue?"
aMiNo needs to restart in order to apply this setting.
Wi-Fi is required. aMiNo will continue running and wait for a Wi-Fi connection before restarting in the background.

The latest version is already installed
aMiNo is already starting in the background
This service is only supported on TV devices

Add the “auth” extra to your intent. You can find your token by tapping “View intents” in the app.
Make sure the token in your intent matches the one shown under “View intents” in the app.
Allow the app to use aMiNo.

aMiNo needs WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS to start on boot. Tap to learn how to grant it.
Watchdog restarted the service. Tap to learn about potential fixes to prevent future crashes.

Lets aMiNo capture the pairing code automatically from the official wireless-debugging pairing screen in Android settings - on phones AND TVs, whenever typing the code is inconvenient. While enabled it reads ONLY the Android settings windows, it never turns itself off, and you can disable it anytime in system settings.

Legacy aMiNo has been deprecated since March 2019. Also, legacy aMiNo does not work on newer Android systems.

Please ask the developer of %1$s to update.

%1$s has modern aMiNo support, but it\'s requesting legacy aMiNo. This could because aMiNo is not running, please check in aMiNo app.

Legacy aMiNo has been deprecated since March 2019.
Open a live terminal directly connected to the device after pairing. The connection stays open.
Chat assistant on Cloudflare Workers AI. Pairing, keys and memory stay in this app.
Pairing and connection succeeded - aMiNo Shell is working!
aMiNo service is running on the device
aMiNo Shell - the connection stays open.\nType a command and press send, or try the experimental options below.\nTry \'help\' to list experimental checks.
The service is running - this window stays open now. Tap SHELL to open the live terminal.

The device is now paired. Start the aMiNo service, then open the Shell terminal - the connection will stay open. Note: Android itself does NOT show any system notification for pairing; aMiNo posts its own status notification (if notifications are allowed).

Real system state of the aMiNo accessibility service (used to capture the wireless-debugging pairing code automatically on phones and TVs). The state below is read live from Android - never from a saved flag. aMiNo never enables it silently, and the service never disables itself.
Real status of every permission aMiNo can use - read live from Android. aMiNo never claims a permission the system did not grant, and root is never required.
Blocked by Android for normal apps
Shows pairing progress and connection status. Android 13+ asks for explicit approval.
Only if a future agent task needs a photo. Nothing runs without it.
Only if a future agent task needs audio recording. Nothing runs without it.
Reads photos and videos your aMiNo commands or agent tasks touch. Official runtime dialog on Android 13+ ("Photos and videos").
Reads audio files your aMiNo commands or agent tasks touch. Official runtime dialog ("Music and audio") - nothing is read without your approval.
Reads media files your aMiNo commands touch. Android 12-and-below storage permission, granted through the official dialog.
Required on Android 13+ to discover the wireless-debugging port via mDNS on the local network.
Optional. Auto-captures the pairing code from the official wireless-debugging pairing screen (phones and TVs). Enabled manually in system settings; it never disables itself.
Keeps the aMiNo server alive across events. Exemption is requested through the official dialog.
Usually NOT needed: aMiNo works with the system file picker and shared storage. Special permission, granted only from system settings.
Allows the in-app update flow to install aMiNo updates. Special permission, granted from system settings.
Not available for normal apps (Android security design)

Signature-level permissions cannot be granted to any normal app. They exist in the manifest only for the adb-granted server path; the UI never fakes them. Official alternative: run the specific command through the aMiNo server (shell channel).
Root is NOT required for aMiNo. Everything runs through the official wireless-debugging pairing and the on-device server.
Paired successfully. Start the service, then the Shell session can connect. (Android itself shows no system notification for pairing.)
The shell session is disconnected. Reconnect from the aMiNo Shell screen.
Granted automatically at install (never asked again)
Special system accesses (official system pages only)
aMiNo does NOT use these (never requested)
Internet and local-network access used for mDNS discovery and the on-device ADB connection. Granted at install, no popup.
Camera, microphone, contacts, location, Bluetooth, phone
aMiNo does not use any of these. They are NOT in the manifest and are never requested. If a future agent feature ever needs one, it will be listed here first with a real request.
Not configured — add an API key
No API key configured. Open the Keys page and add one.
Too many tool steps for one task — stopped for safety.
Autonomous task — describe the goal; the agent plans, executes and self-corrects step by step…
Why: %1$s. It was NOT executed yet. Allow it?
Could not build a valid plan from the model (no parseable JSON). Try rephrasing the goal.
Could not generate the final report.
The run stopped early: too many failures or a required command is not allowed on this device.
You output ONLY valid JSON objects. No markdown, no explanations.
You are AMINO\'s report writer. Honest, concrete, based only on provided real results.
Delete the encrypted key stored on this device?
Saved locally, encrypted with Android Keystore
Could not encrypt (Keystore error) — nothing was saved

The key is stored ONLY on this phone, encrypted with the hardware Android Keystore. It is sent exclusively to your chosen model provider as the request authentication header. It never appears in logs, prompts, or crash reports.

Cloudflare Workers AI (recommended — works in every country): 1) dash.cloudflare.com → Workers & Pages → copy the Account ID and paste it in the Base URL replacing ACCOUNT_ID. 2) Create an API Token (My Profile → API Tokens, or Workers AI page → Use REST API) and paste it as the API key. 3) Pick a model, e.g. @cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct or @cf/qwen/qwen2.5-32b-instruct (strong Arabic).
Google Gemini requires a key from a supported country; if your region is blocked (e.g. Algeria) the request will fail with "User location is not supported" — use Cloudflare Workers AI instead.
